english: Grandmother, why are the women weeping? Your mother's father has died, little one. Will he not come back? He will not come back. He has gone to the fathers, and he sits with them. What are the women singing? They are singing his name. His name will be famous. I will sing it too. Sing, child, and he will hear you.

english: Grandmother, my little child does not breathe. Why did the gods carry the child off? I do not know, my child. I too gave two sons to the earth. How did you live afterwards? Grief lay on my heart a whole year. Then your mother was born, and I rejoiced again. Will I rejoice again? You will rejoice. Now shed your tears, and I will hold you.

english: Our old dog is lying at grandmother's stone. He does not eat. Grief holds him. She fed him with her own hands. Do dogs know death? They know it. A dog's heart is true. Shall I bring him food there? Bring it to him, and call him. Will he follow me? He will follow you when the sun goes down.

english: Widow of the chief, what song of praise shall I chant for him? Praise him: 'He gave cows to the guests, and he did not fear the enemy.' Did he suffer at the end? He did not suffer at the end. He lay down in the evening, and sleep took him. Then I will praise his fame at the feast. May his fame be imperishable. What reward do you want? I do not want a reward. I loved him.

english: "Let this be so," said the bright god Werunos.

english: Sister, I have heard of your grief. When did your husband leave you? He left me at dawn, and I was alone. Your husband was a good man. He used to give me milk in the winter. He was good to everyone. Now his fire has gone cold. Do not weep alone. The women will sing for you. Sing, and I will pour mead for him.

english: Father-in-law, the year has gone away. Grass is growing on my husband's stone. Grass grows, and grief becomes small. My grief has not become small. I see his shadow at the door. I too see it. Sit at the hearth, and let us two speak his name. Let us speak it, and let us laugh. He was glad at this hearth.

english: Master of the house, I come from another village. Why are the women wailing in your house? My wife is dead, guest. Come in, and eat with us. Your grief is great. Shall I go away? Do not go. A guest is holy. Sit, and tell us of your road. I will tell it, and I will praise your wife's name. You are dear to me.

english: Sister, I am afraid of the dead man. He does not breathe. Do not tremble before him, brother. He is the old man who used to carry you. Why does he not look at me? He lies in a long sleep. Kiss his face, and say to him: 'Be well.' Be well. He hears you.

english: Do you remember the song which mother sang at the loom? I remember it; I hear it in my heart. Sing it for me. I am an old man, and my voice is heavy. You sing it: you are her daughter. I will sing it, and you will listen. I am listening. Now she sings again with your voice.

english: The Sheep and the Horses

english: Friend, my breath is weak. Will you guard my children when I am gone? I will guard them. May Sky and Earth hear my oath. Your word is strong; now I am not afraid. Give my knife to the first of the children when he has grown up. I will give it to him, and I will tell him your name. Shall I call your brothers? Call them.

english: Grandfather, tell me a story of your brother. My brother was a shepherd, and he had many horses. In the winter a wolf came, and the shepherd killed it with a stone. Where does your brother lie now? He lies in the earth over there, and a pillar stands for him. Will you show me the pillar? I will show it to you in the morning. Remember him: then he lives.

english: Husband, I saw my mother in a dream. What did she say to you? She said nothing. She was standing at the hearth, and she was looking at me. Was she angry? She was not angry. She wanted to see her own daughter. Shall I give her something? Give her a cup of sweet mead, and speak her name. I will do so, and may she come in my dreams.

english: King's daughter, I have come home from the fight. Where is the king? The king has lain under the stone for three nights. Was he asking for me? He was asking for you, and he left you his own blade. I do not deserve it. He chose you. Take it, and protect the people with it. I vow it. May Sky hear your vow.

english: Friend, you have not eaten for three days. Eat this meat which I cooked. Hunger does not hold me. My heart burned with my wife on the fire. She loved you; she does not want your death. You speak the truth, friend. Give me the meat; I will eat. Did you cook it yourself? I cooked it. Eat, and live for your daughters.

pie: ǵŕ̥h₂enti moy ḱéh₂desos kéh₂nmn̥ kh₂né. tód ne wóydh₂e. nu ḱléwse. kʷíd príHe n̥smé léykʷs? nu nos kʷís h₂Hséh₂i sédyēti. tód solh₂wóm kéh₂nmn̥? tód ne solh₂wóm kéh₂nmn̥. tód solh₂wéh₂m nókʷtm̥ kh₂nómes. tód tébʰye ḱóm kh₂nṓh₂. kh₂né dáḱruh₂-kʷe toy mē ḱéles.
english: Old woman, sing me the song of grief. I do not know it. Listen, then. 'Why did you leave us, dear one? Who will sit at our hearth now?' Is that the whole song? That is not the whole song. We chant it through the whole night. I will chant it with you. Chant, and do not hide your tears.

english: Wife, our son has been born. Which name shall we set on him? Let us set on him the name of my father, Of-Good-Fame. He left us in the winter and did not see the boy. He was a kindly man. Will the little one carry his name? He will carry it, and his name will be good. Then let us say his name at the hearth this evening. Let us say it, and may the gods hear it.

english: Where has my uncle gone? He has gone along the dark path to the dead. Is the path long? It is long, but he does not walk alone. The gods lead him. Will he be hungry there? He will not be hungry there. We gave him grain and meat. I will give him my foal. Keep your foal, child. He gave it to you.

pie: kʷóti gʰósteyes h₁súmenes dh₂pnóm gʷm̥sḱṓnti? ḱm̥tóm wiHrṓs tóysōm-kʷe pótnih₂es. mḗms méǵh₂i kʷéroy pékʷe. uksnés mḗms bʰr̥ǵyṓh₂? tód h₂éydʰoy bʰr̥ǵyé h₁n̥gʷnéyey-kʷe sélpos dh₃dʰí. kʷíd h₁édmes h₁yód nos ḱéh₂dos séǵʰeti? néḱus n̥sméy ḱóm h₁ḗdti gʷíh₃womes-kʷe. médʰu wédʰesi? tód wédʰoh₂.
english: Kindly One, how many guests will come to the feast? A hundred men and their wives. Cook the meat in the great cauldron. Shall I roast the bull's flesh? Roast it on the fire, and give the fat to Fire. Why do we eat when grief holds us? The dead man eats with us, and we live. Are you bringing the mead? I am bringing it.

pie: kʷíd swéḱruh₂ h₁n̥gʷním kʷsépi h₂élesi? snúse ḱós h₁n̥gʷnís sh₂krós. ḱósyo déms pótnih₂es tóm ḱm̥tóm yéh₁ōr h₂élont. h₁yód stéwdeti? nu nos mr̥tṓs stéwdonti. dʰuh₂mós dyḗm úd yéh₂ti só tóysōm stóygʰos. nu h₁eǵóh₂ tóm h₂élōh₂. nu túH ḱósyo déms pótnih₂. h₂ewsér stéh₂esi? h₂ewsér stéh₂oh₂ tóm-kʷe h₂élōh₂.
english: Mother-in-law, why do you feed the fire at night? This fire is holy, daughter-in-law. The mistresses of this house have fed it for a hundred years. And if it grows cold? Then our dead grow cold. The smoke goes up to the sky: it is their road. Then I too will feed it. Then you are a mistress of this house. Will you rise at dawn? I will rise at dawn and feed it.
